answer: Trust-Weighted Clique Retention. An agent's trust is capped by the size of its largest mutually-consistent neighbor clique; edges require bidirectional work, so fake neighbors form only a sparse signal. When a node's clique collapses on removal tests, its trust enters a decay spiral. Any new identity starts near zero and must earn a whisper of trust from established cliques, costing an attacker a full re-acquisition of verifiable peer work per identity.
